newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso falls on unexpected oil demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso falls on unexpected oil demand.

text.p: * Market caught off guard on $23.5 million requirement
A surprise $23.5-million demand by an oil company sent banks looking for dollars and weakened the Philippine peso at the close on Friday, traders said.
The peso ended at 26.235 pesos to the dollar from 26.223. The day's average was at 26.231 compared with Thursday's 26.222.
Volume narrowed to $93 million from $132.48 million.
"It caused panic buying. No one knew about it until everyone squared their positions," said a foreign bank dealer.
A dealer said the oil company announced its requirement 15 minutes before banks were scheduled to sell about $7 million to oil companies in the afternoon.
The sudden demand caught banks off guard since most had already sold the dollar inflows that came in the morning, he said.
The peso fell to a low of 26.237 pesos, far off its intraday high of 26.222 pesos.
Next week, the direction of the peso would be dictated by any moves the Central Bank would make on its overnight rates after cutting it by 1.5 percent points last Monday, traders said.
